instruction: Using VLC and GIMP, generate an animated GIF named final_animation.gif from the video src.mp4 on the Desktop. The GIF should be a 5-second clip starting from 00:01.

metadata.explanation: Task creates a 5-second animated GIF from video using VLC and GIMP. Process: 1) Open src.mp4 in VLC, 2) Seek to 1-second position, 3) Extract 5-second clip, 4) Import frames to GIMP, 5) Export as final_animation.gif. Evaluator checks file exists, is GIF format, and has at least 10 frames.

scoring_breakdown.0.5: GIF file exists at specified location

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Cannot verify the 5-second duration requirement - evaluator only checks frame count (min_frames: 10) but doesn't verify actual GIF duration
CRITICAL: Cannot verify the clip starts at 00:01 timestamp - no mechanism to check the temporal starting point from source video
CRITICAL: Cannot verify the GIF was created from src.mp4 - any GIF file at the target path would pass
Frame count check (min_frames: 10) makes assumptions about frame rate - 5 seconds could be 10 frames at 2fps, 25 at 5fps, or 50 at 10fps
Evaluator only verifies basic properties (file exists, is GIF format, has animation) but misses core temporal requirements
Incomplete coverage: instruction has 5 key requirements but evaluator only checks 3 basic ones (file name/location, format, animation)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add duration verification: getter should extract GIF duration from metadata (e.g., using PIL to calculate total_duration = sum of all frame durations), metric should check duration is approximately 5 seconds (±0.5s tolerance)
Consider adding frame rate check: if 5 seconds is expected, validate frame count matches expected duration (e.g., 5s * estimated_fps should equal frame_count ± tolerance)
Add expected duration to config: expected: {min_frames: 10, duration_seconds: 5.0, duration_tolerance: 0.5}

Note: Verifying the exact starting timestamp (00:01) from source video is infeasible without analyzing video content - consider simplifying the instruction to remove this requirement or accept that it cannot be automatically verified
Alternative: If temporal verification is critical, could extract first frame from GIF and compare with frame at 00:01 from src.mp4 using image similarity, but this adds significant complexity
